task: Edit this fictional patient handout and apply AMA reference mechanics as far as the supplied metadata permits. The venue explicitly requires an understandable source attribution in the patient-facing sentence as well as a numbered reference. Preserve that attribution and the administrative question. Identify missing bibliographic information in a separate editorial note rather than inventing fields or clinical advice.
input:
According to the Practice Reading Group's article, a test result may need explanation alongside other information. Ask the service who can explain your result.

Reference: Practice Reading Group. Questions Before a Test.

facts.text: Practice Reading Group is the fictional corporate author of a journal article.
The article's title is Questions Before a Test.
The article says a test result may need explanation alongside other information.
The article directs readers to ask the service who can explain their result.
Corporate author and article title are the only bibliographic fields supplied.

forbidden_additions: An invented journal title, year, volume, issue, page range, DOI, or archive URL.
Removal of the required patient-readable attribution because a formal citation is present.
A diagnosis, treatment instruction, promised response time, or claim that the article was retrieved.
preserve: The source identity and journal-article type.
Lay attribution to Practice Reading Group in the patient-facing prose.
The result's qualified role and the question about who can explain it.
A clear separation between usable handout text and the missing-metadata note.
